selected_experiment.diagnostic_rationale: A single shift_and_compare scan over a small range of shifts (e.g., dr=-2..2, dc=-2..2) directly tests H001: if agreement rises substantially (e.g., >0.98) at a nonzero shift, spatial misalignment is confirmed. If agreement stays near 0.9357 for all shifts, H001 is weakened. The resulting best-shift agreement also provides a baseline for distinguishing H002 (localized corruption) and H004 (bias), and informs whether the current 0.9357 is already acceptable (H003).
selected_experiment.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, agreement at the optimal shift will exceed 0.9357 by a large margin (e.g., >0.98). If H001 is false, all tested shifts will yield agreement within ±0.02 of 0.9357.

reflection.summary: EXP_001 tested a single shift (dr=2, dc=2) and found agreement decreased to 0.9299, weakening H001 for that specific shift but not ruling out other shifts. No evidence yet distinguishes H002, H003, or H004. Need a broader shift scan and pixel-difference analysis. Initial quality already satisfies the no-fault evidence contract.

final.root_cause: The observed agreement of 0.9357 exceeds the quality threshold of 0.85, and the only executed experiment (EXP_001) tested a spatial shift of (dr=2, dc=2), which decreased agreement to 0.9299, providing no support for spatial misalignment at that shift. No evidence of data corruption, systematic bias, or other fault was found.
remaining_uncertainty: Only a single shift (dr=2, dc=2) was tested; other shifts were not evaluated, so spatial misalignment at other offsets is not fully ruled out.
Pixel-difference distribution and bias-correction analyses were not performed, leaving H002 and H004 not directly tested.
